text:
spike-bot: Alert — unusual pattern detected: rapid short-lived SSO sessions from alternating user agents across multiple orgs (eu-west). 28 auth attempts, 18 MFA prompts, 12 failures in last 10m. https://dash.redwood.internal/alerts/2109876543

maya (secops): saw this, correlating with a bump in session revokes. looks like a probe trying to generate MFA fatigue rather than a single credential compromise.

kevin (auth): @maya can you paste a sample of the headers you pulled? I'm seeing UA rotation and small IP hops consistent with proxy chains.

maya (secops): sample headers for acct alice@acme.example:
```
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) Chrome/111.0
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 15_4 like Mac OS X) Mobile/15E148
X-Forwarded-For: 34.202.12.45, 54.10.1.2
```

sam (oncall): started targeted session revokes for top-12 affected users. cmd used: `redwoodctl sessions revoke --filter 'recent_auth_probe=true' --reason 'auth-probe-detect'`. Audit events emitted.

kevin (auth): WAF rule pushed to block suspicious UA hash. added candidate proxy IP ranges to denylist; soft throttle applied to SSO endpoint (rate-limit + 429 backoff).

maya (secops): pinging CSM @lia-core — any customers reporting repeated MFA prompts? need to prepare comms. :rotating_light:

lia-core: CSMs saw a ticket from AcmeEdge about multiple prompts ~10:12 UTC. I'll draft an admin-facing note and warn tenants to rotate service keys if they see unexpected prompts.

maya (secops): KMS check — any anomalous key usage? @nina (sec-eng) can you sweep KMS audit?

nina (sec-eng): KMS logs show no unusual Decrypt/Sign calls from service accounts in the window. No extraneous key material access. Recommend rotating ephemeral worker keys for the affected pool as a precaution. Filed INFRA-4567.

kevin (auth): triage notes: this appears to be abuse/probing; no evidence of token theft or key misuse. Post-incident actions I propose:
- fingerprinting: detect alternating-browser-chain UA flip within short windows
- surface per-user MFA-prompt counters in Console
- hard rate-limits on initial SSO flows + exponential backoff
I'll open RFC-Auth-210 to track.

sam (oncall): recorded remediation in incident tracker INC-2109. Will do follow-ups and escalate to legal if any orgs request audit packages.

maya (secops): audit/logging: we should bump auth event retention for 90 days for compliance/customer requests. ops team, can you evaluate cost impact?

ops-team-bot: Noted. Created ticket OPS-9823 to evaluate retention, cold storage, and cost estimates.

kevin (auth): vuln triage: anything indicating exploit chain? token replay? session fixation?

maya (secops): initial checks — no token reuse seen in our nonce logs. Assigning @oliver (runtime) to validate replay protections.

oliver (runtime): validated nonce and sequence checks, no replays. runtime caches show only short-lived sessions created and expired as expected. closing that line.

maya (secops): customer comms: @lia-core please include recommended defensive steps (rotate org API keys, enforce per-user device MFA app checks). Also include our mitigations and ETA for full postmortem.

lia-core: will send draft to legal + ops for approval.

kevin (auth): ops change: add a small RBAC tweak request — allow secops to trigger org-wide session revokes without SRE runway. It speeds containment. Need product signoff. I'll draft the request.

maya (secops): agreed. security team should not be blocked on 3rd party SRE for immediate revokes. Add to postmortem actions.

sam (oncall): schedule 30-min postmortem tomorrow 09:30 UTC. attendees: @kevin, @maya, @nina, @oliver, @lia-core, @sam.

spike-bot: Alert cleared — probe volume back to baseline.

maya (secops): thanks all. short-term checklist created in INC-2109. Will publish notes after RFC and retention cost estimate.
